reason: FAQ quote states existing IAM roles or users continue to function as-is after enabling, so migration can be phased without disrupting existing access.
Quote states that after signing in to the AWS access portal a user can get temporary credentials and use them in the AWS CLI or AWS SDKs to access resources in an AWS account.
Quote states it is deployed to the currently selected Region, called the primary Region, which cannot be changed after enabling.
FAQ quote states identities from an existing IdP must be provisioned into IAM Identity Center before you can assign permissions.
Table row gives default quota 7000, can be increased Yes; the footnote in context says it applies separately to accounts and to applications.
Row under Active Directory quotas: connected directories at a time 1, can be increased No.
Row under identity store quotas: groups supported 100000, can be increased Yes.
Row: groups assignable to a permission set per AWS account, or to an application, 100, can be increased No.
Quote states quota increase requests must come from a management or delegated administrator account.
Row: inline policies per permission set 1, can be increased No.
Row gives 32,768 bytes maximum inline policy size and 10,240 bytes of non-whitespace characters, can be increased No.
Row: instances of IAM Identity Center per account 1, can be increased No.
Row: permission sets allowed 3500, can be increased Yes.
Row: provisioned permission sets per AWS account 500, can be increased Yes.
Row: Regions enabled for a single instance 6 as the default quota, can be increased Yes.
Row under Application quotas: SAML assertion limit 50,000 characters, can be increased No.
Row: total number of trusted token issuers 10, can be increased No.
Row under identity store quotas: users supported 200000, can be increased Yes.
FAQ quote states an existing RADIUS MFA configuration can be used with IAM Identity Center and AWS Directory Services as a secondary form of verification.
FAQ quote calls it the recommended front door into AWS and says it should be the primary tool to manage workforce access.
Both quotes state the Region must be accessible by all users for account SSO and that most AWS managed applications require Identity Center in the same Region.
Quote states replication to additional Regions maintains account access with already provisioned permissions in a Regional disruption.
Quote states replication automatically copies users, groups, permission sets and their assignments, and other metadata and configuration.

Quotes support that the deny policy is assumed to be in an SCP, that otherwise an active role session gets its actions back, and that sessions expire after 12 hours; no quote or context says the procedure adds the user's ID to the Deny policy, and 'at least 12 hours' is only in an unquoted step heading.
Quote states IAM role sessions operate independently once established and persist for the duration configured in the permission set, up to 12 hours, regardless of the sign-in session.
Quotes state roles beginning with AWSReservedSSO_ were created by the service from assigning a permission set to the account.

The quotes support Client VPN integrating exclusively through SAML, but the OAuth 2.0 data-access ability is stated only in the context of connecting an existing IdP (and, in the next bullet, JWT support via trusted identity propagation); the claim states it unconditionally, and the 'assign access to SAML 2.0 applications' sentence is context, not a quote.
Quote states it can authenticate and authorize access to SAML-based customer managed apps reachable through a public URL regardless of platform or cloud.
FAQ quote states a supported SAML 2.0 IdP source uses the provider's MFA, and with Identity Center or AD as source it supports WebAuthn security keys and built-in biometric authenticators.
Quote states the Subject NameID must exactly match the Username and sign-in fails otherwise even when the IdP authenticates the user.
Quotes state automatic provisioning with SCIM v2.0, configured in the IdP with the SCIM endpoint and a bearer token created in IAM Identity Center.
FAQ quote names Okta Universal Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, OneLogin and PingFederate synchronized automatically with SCIM.
Quote states the IdP controls SCIM provisioning and update intervals and changes appear only after the IdP sends them.
Quote, under the User-initiated heading, states application sessions end within approximately 30 minutes at next refresh and IAM role sessions continue until expiry, up to 12 hours later.
Two quotes state Samba 4-based Simple AD is not supported as an identity source or as a connected directory.
FAQ quote lists user and group attributes, assignment metadata for accounts and applications, and granted permissions for account access.

Quotes define temporary elevated access as just-in-time request, approve and track for a task and time, and state IAM Identity Center integrates with AWS Security Competency partner solutions on that page.
Quote states throttle limits apply equally to each enabled Region for a multi-Region instance.

Quote states trusted identity propagation is built on OAuth 2.0 and can exchange external authorization server tokens for Identity Center tokens recognized by AWS services; the same bullet says this lets the app request data access on behalf of users.

Quotes state identity context is added to an IAM role and propagated, administrators grant permissions on user attributes such as group associations, and can audit who accessed what data in service logs or CloudTrail.
